promo-wall-crop.title: Your phone crops 18% off your wallpaper #shorts
promo-wall-crop.description:
Almost every wallpaper template is 1080 x 1920 — sixteen by nine. Your phone is nineteen-and-a-half by nine, and it never letterboxes: it fills the height and crops the width. That is about 18% gone on an iPhone 16 Pro or a Galaxy S25, and over 20% on a Pixel. Design at 1440 x 3120 instead and every phone scales it down. Full wallpaper guide on the channel.

promo-wall-safezone.title: The one band of your wallpaper that is actually visible #shorts
promo-wall-safezone.description:
Your phone screen is never empty. A clock and date own the top third, app icons sit through the middle and a dock owns the bottom. Only the middle band is reliably yours. The ten-second check: rectangles over the top quarter and bottom fifth at half transparency — what is left is your real canvas. Full wallpaper guide on the channel.

#canva #wallpaper #canvatips #design

promo-clock-eats-subject.title: The iPhone clock is eating your wallpaper #shorts
promo-clock-eats-subject.description:
On the iOS lock screen the depth effect may put your subject behind the clock, or refuse to, and it is not a setting you control. It depends on the picture having a clear subject with space around it. Leave a clean gap under the clock and it usually behaves — and if it does not, move the subject lower. That is genuinely the whole fix.

promo-cannot-sell-stock.title: You cannot sell a Canva stock photo #shorts
promo-cannot-sell-stock.description:
From Canva's Content Licence Agreement: you cannot sell "standalone prints of Canva content, such as a printout of a stock photo without any other design elements". A stock photo exported at wallpaper size is exactly that. Sell your own original design instead. Not legal advice — read the current licence yourself before you list anything.
